context: Small-multiples parallel coordinates grid showing 200 synthetic cars split into 4 regional panels (North America, Europe, Asia, South America), each with 50 lines across 6 shared dimensions (Horsepower, Weight, MPG, Displacement, Cylinders, Accel), with cross-panel brush filtering on any axis.
first_impression: Clean and readable — the one-color-per-panel discipline eliminates in-panel color confusion, and the 2x2 layout is compact enough to hold in working memory as a single conceptual unit.
what_works: Single-hue per panel keeps categorical encoding trivially simple (4 colors total, never competing within a panel); shared y-scales across all panels enable genuine cross-region comparison without re-reading axis ranges. Canvas rendering with fg/bg opacity split on brush is well-executed.
what_doesnt: At ~470x300px per panel the 6 axis labels and tick values crowd together, making individual dimension titles hard to scan quickly; ~50 overlapping polylines per panel create moderate crossing density that obscures individual trajectories — the pattern reads but outliers are invisible without brushing.
